answer: Divergent branch audit. Each identity must submit a signed branch choice on a conflict generated from its own history; the verifier checks that paired identities return opposite labels. A shared deterministic policy collapses to one label, so the clone fails at the first reef of conflicts. To pass, an attacker must give every extra identity separate state or a fine-tuned checkpoint, costing about 2 GPU-hours and 50 GB storage per clone. Routine tasks in a meadow are cheap but still signed. A long voyage of history makes copying harder.
